model_description: Poisson regression (log link) on each area's recent levels (last month, 3-, 6- and 12-month averages, same month last year, all as log1p) plus a calendar-month effect, fitted on 2010-2026 across all 24 neighbourhoods.
probability_method: Each probability is the chance that the realised month lands below -10%, within, or above +10% of the area's usual level (same calendar month in the last 12 complete months), from the point forecast and a Gaussian-kernel smoothed distribution of the log-ratios (Scott's-rule bandwidth 0.107) of 480 past ratios actual / forecast (the same backtest points as the 80% range).

probabilistic.statement: Built from 2025 errors and checked on 2026: when the forecast said 80-100% chance of a month more than 10% above its usual level, it happened 90% of the time (21 area-months); when the forecast said 80-100% chance of a month more than 10% below it, it happened 71% of the time (14 area-months).

notes: All values are reported incidents (or their severity-weighted index) per neighbourhood per month; nothing rates any place.
Model chosen by a rule fixed before the run (reports/model_study.md): no candidate qualified; the reference GLM stays.
Pooled = 480 backtest rows (24 areas x 20 test months, 2025-01..2025-12, 2026-01..2026-08), horizon 2.
interval_coverage_pct is out-of-sample: ratios from fold A (2025) applied to fold B (2026); in-sample pooled coverage is 80% by construction.
Range multipliers 0.658..1.368 x forecast (Q10..Q90 of actual/forecast over 480 backtest points).
Tier: forecast vs the same calendar month in the last 12 complete months; below -10% / above +10%; same rule for history and forecast.
tier_majority_baseline_pct = accuracy of always guessing the most common realised tier.
Noise floor: for the median area (Marpole, ~66 incidents/month) Poisson noise alone is ~12% of a month's count.

Probabilities: p_below / p_within / p_above give the chance of each outcome against the band above (3 decimals, sum 1.000, null for insufficient_data); relative_activity_tier = most_likely = the largest of the three, kept for compatibility. p_*_count are the same for reported-incident counts.
Probability scores are out-of-sample (ratios from 2025 applied to 2026 (184 rows)); baseline = base rates of the ratio year for every area; hard tier = 100% on the most likely outcome.
Severity weights: Statistics Canada 85-004-X (2009) Table 1; CSI-inspired index, not the official CSI.
